results.correct_value: gain_ft 7680 (car to car from Killen Creek, matching loss_ft and the itinerary total)
results.evidence: Inside the row, loss_ft (7680), the itinerary gain total (2900+4780=7680), the itinerary loss total (7680) and the trailhead (4,600 ft) and summit (12,276 ft) pins all describe a ~7,700 ft car-to-car outing; gain_ft 5150 matches only the camp-to-summit climb (a route-only figure of ~4,700-5,000 ft). A 2011 Adams Glacier trip report from the Killen Creek trailhead gives 8,000 ft of gain car to car, agreeing with the row's ~7,700 ft rather than 5,150. No second source states a car-to-car figure for this route, so the row's own itinerary total is adopted rather than a new number.

results.correct_value: Day 1 gain ~2,300 ft (4,600 ft trailhead to ~6,900 ft High Camp); day 2 carries the remaining gain so the itinerary total stays 7,680
results.evidence: itinerary.days[0].gainFt says 2900 while approach ('~2,300-2,500 ft of gain to camp'), approach_variants[0].gainFt (2300) and the trailhead/High Camp elevations (4,600 -> 6,900 ft) say ~2,300. The Killen Creek to High Camp hike page gives 2,300 ft of gain with a 6,900 ft high point, and an independent Adams Glacier trip report gives the trailhead at c.4,600 ft and the end of the High Camp Trail at c.6,900 ft. Day 2 is raised by the same 600 ft (camp 6,900 -> summit 12,276 is ~5,376 ft), so the itinerary total remains 7,680 = gain_ft.

Two sources agree the glacier's terminus (toe) is at about 7,000 ft (the Killen Creek hike page: 'terminus of the glacier at 7,000 feet'; the Adams Glacier encyclopedia entry), which supports approach/approach_variants. But the waypoint describes where parties rope up after a ~two-hour leg, and trip reports put the rope-up point at ~8,000 ft (2014), ~8,500 ft (EBC), a flat area ~8,000 ft (Hebert) and ~9,000 ft (2011) — they do not agree on one figure, and setting the pin to 7,000 would contradict its own two-hour description. To settle: decide whether the pin marks the terminus (then 7,000 ft, sourced) or the rope-up point (then reword its directions from 'glacier toe' and find a second report agreeing on ~8,000 ft).

results.correct_value: Itinerary days: day 1 +2,300 ft; day 2 +5,391/-5,390 ft; day 3 -2,300 ft (totals 7,691 / 7,690 = gain_ft / loss_ft)
results.evidence: Two independent North Ridge/North Cleaver sources give car-to-car gain of 7,800 ft (Killen Creek, 17 mi) and 8,160 ft (20 mi, starting lower because of snow), both consistent with gain_ft 7,691 and contradicting the itinerary's 6,200 ft. The Killen Creek to High Camp hike page gives 2,300 ft of gain to a 6,900 ft high point (matching approach_variants gainFt 2300 and the bivy note), so day 1's 2,900 and day 3's 2,900 loss were overstated, and day 2 (6,900 -> 12,276 ft and back) was understated at 3,300. The corrected days sum exactly to the stored gain_ft and loss_ft.

Only the Mountaineers (route page and activity page, one author) state Grade II, agreeing with alpine_grade, commitment and rope_note. Mountain Project gives only 'Mod. Snow'; the Mazamas page uses its own letter scale (D). No second independent commitment grade was found, and only three fields oppose the outlier. To settle: a second guide (e.g. a printed Cascade guide) giving the route's commitment grade.

Mountain Project says the route is climbed in late spring (supports May-Jun); the Mazamas list it for both spring and summer (supports running into July). Neither states a month window, so they do not agree on one value. To settle: a source that names the months the route is in condition.

The Mountaineers gear list gives 4-5 long screws and 2 pickets (matching sling_rack/rack). Mountain Project says only that the route is protectable with pickets/snow anchors and a running belay, with no counts; the Mazamas page lists no gear. No second source gives counts. To settle: a second gear list with screw and picket counts.

gain_ft and loss_ft are 5000 (matching Mountain Project's route-only 5,000 ft), while the itinerary totals 6,700 ft gain and 6,700 ft loss, and the trailhead (4,600) to summit (12,276) pins imply ~7,700 ft car to car; the Mazamas state 7,800 ft of gain from the trailhead for this route. Only one source gives a car-to-car figure, and day 1's 2,900 also disagrees with the sourced ~2,300 ft to High Camp. To settle: a second source stating the car-to-car gain for the Lyman Glacier route.
